FR-001.title: A person raising a request MUST choose a Category, and then an Item, in that order.

FR-002.title: The Item step MUST offer the Items the requesting job supports plus the job-independent Items and MUST never be empty; unsupported Items MUST NOT appear at all, because the check runs before the choice.

FR-003.title: No screen may offer a request type or a subtype, and the wizard type and subtype steps MUST be gone.

FR-004.title: A stored request MUST carry the chosen Category and Item, and MUST NOT carry a request type or a subtype.

FR-005.title: Every request renders as one card whose first line is the Item umbrella phrase and whose second line is the Item identifier.

FR-006.title: The card MUST use one layout for every Item; no layout variant may be selected by Item.

FR-007.title: An Item own fields MUST appear on the request page and MUST NOT appear on the card.

FR-008.title: The card MUST keep the four metadata rows: who asked, the work centre, the time remaining, and how long it has waited.

FR-009.title: A card picture MUST be the Item picture, falling back to the Category picture only when the Item has none; a placeholder MUST NOT replace a resolved picture.

FR-010.title: The list MUST default to most-urgent-first.

FR-011.title: A viewer MUST be able to change the sort from a control beside the existing shell controls, and the choice MUST be remembered.

FR-012.title: Overdue requests MUST remain visibly marked as overdue whatever the sort.

FR-013.title: An Item behaviour MUST come from stored configuration rather than from compiled-in code.

FR-014.title: Every Item MUST have a configuration row, and an Item with no row MUST be reported as unavailable rather than half-configured.

FR-015.title: An Item configuration MUST be changeable without a code change and without a rebuild.

FR-016.title: A request deadline MUST be derived from its Item allotted minutes, never from a type or subtype.

FR-017.title: An Item with no configured minutes MUST use a 15-minute default, labelled as a default.

FR-018.title: The minutes screen MUST show, per Item, its configured minutes and the average its completed requests actually took, as visibly distinct values.

FR-019.title: The average MUST count only completed requests from acceptance to completion, a released-then-completed request contributing exactly once.

FR-020.title: Both configuration screens MUST reuse the role gate that already governs them and MUST NOT introduce a new one.

FR-021.title: An Item picture MUST be configurable per Item, and a nothing-configured answer MUST NOT replace a resolved image.

FR-022.title: Every user-visible string introduced or changed MUST come from the existing resource mechanism.

FR-023.title: The request type and subtype vocabulary, its catalogs, seed, read procedure and the services named for it MUST be removed, and the schema master lists kept in sync.

FR-024.title: Every data operation MUST go through a stored procedure; no inline statement text may be introduced.

FR-025.title: Every schema artifact added, changed or removed MUST ship with its matching rollback, and the master lists kept in sync.

FR-026.title: An unavailable Item, a refused action or a failed read MUST be reported in plain actionable language; nothing may fail silently.

FR-027.title: The per-Item field definitions MUST come solely from the request-configuration spreadsheet, and the application MUST NOT read, embed or ship it.

FR-028.title: The four Items whose value source does not exist yet MUST NOT be offered until that work lands.

FR-029.title: The wrong-material Items MUST each read as a single Deliver request whose second line carries the correct material identifier.

FR-030.title: The Scrap Item value MUST be the scrap type already set on the job; the user MUST NOT be asked to enter it.

FR-031.title: The Scrap Item MUST be offered only when the job has a real scrap decision, not No Scrap and not the Scrap Type Required placeholder.

FR-032.title: Choosing an Item MUST NOT change the request lifecycle: statuses, transitions and who may perform them stay exactly as they are.

intent: Let a person raise a request by naming the Category and Item they actually mean, and let every request read as the same two-line card whatever it is.
expectations: The four Items with no value source — finished goods, NCM, WIP and outside service — are hidden until their own spec lands.
The defect-types editor is not part of this specification.
The real material identifiers (coil or part number, quantity, stock location) stay deferred to the later item-resolution work.
No migration path is written: the database is reinstalled from seed, and the reinstall is the owner action.
Releasing a request keeps no screen control; it remains service-only.
Verifying with the in-app inspector is superseded by the scripted UI tests.
approach: Re-key the half-built Category/Item layer onto the store rather than rebuild it: add one configuration table row per Item holding behaviour and allotted minutes, re-key the request row and its three procedures to category + item, collapse the seven per-type cards into the one WaitlistLineCardView with no Item-based layout variant, and re-key both Settings screens and the image scope from subtype to Item. The per-Item allotted minutes move out of per-Windows-user local settings into seeded data so the configured value and the observed average can sit side by side; the 15-minute fallback stays app-side and is labelled as a default. The database is reinstalled from seed, so the retiring catalog is consumed at design time and no migration is written.

decisions.decision: One new table waitlist_request_item_configs, one row per Item, holding both the flow behaviour and allotted_minutes
decisions.why: FR-014 is one configuration row per Item in the singular; keeping behaviour and minutes on the same row removes the half-configured state the requirement forbids, and consolidates metadata that the retiring design split across waitlist_request_types and waitlist_request_subtypes
decisions.rejected: A second waitlist_request_item_settings table (creates a half-configured state for one integer column); re-keying waitlist_request_subtypes in place (FR-023 requires its removal); leaving the flow in code (FR-013/FR-015 require it to change as data)

decisions.decision: The card Line 1 and Line 2 stay properties of the code catalog (RequestItemDefinition gains CardLine2Template); the configuration table holds only behaviour
decisions.why: Seed section 16.3 keeps existence, order, Category, umbrella verb and Line 2 in the code catalog, and FR-013 list of what must come from stored configuration excludes the card lines; the retiring type/subtype rows never carried a line-2 template, so moving one there would be new behaviour rather than a re-key
decisions.rejected: A line2_template column on the configuration table (contradicts 16.3 and leaves two owners); deriving Line 2 from ProducedValue (that is the stored value, not the displayed identifier)

decisions.decision: The per-Item allotted minutes move out of ILocalSettingsService into the seeded store, and the 15-minute fallback stays an app-side constant labelled as a default
decisions.why: FR-018 puts the configured value beside the observed average, which is a history read through a stored procedure, and FR-024 forbids inline SQL; a configured value keyed to a Windows user profile is invisible to everyone else and cannot be compared meaningfully with a shared observed value
decisions.rejected: Keeping local settings and adding a DB read only for the average (compares a per-user value with a shared one); per-user minutes in the database (no requirement asks for it and FR-020 already means one configuration for everyone)

decisions.decision: The job-independent Item set is five (both Riser Tables, both Hoppers, other) and a Category that would offer no Item is itself not offered
decisions.why: The spec Edge Case states five after the scrap correction while seed section 16.4 still says six, and the spec is the authority; filtering the Category list is the only way FR-002 must-never-be-empty and SC-005 at-least-one-in-every-case both hold, because none of the five belongs to Assist, whose three Items each require a part on the job
decisions.rejected: Showing an empty Assist Item step with a message (contradicts FR-002 and SC-005); adding a job-independent Assist Item (changes the 23-row catalog the spec pins verbatim); counting Scrap as job-independent (the exact mistake the spec was refreshed to fix)

decisions.decision: The sort preference is per viewer through the existing ILocalSettingsService behind a new IWaitlistSortPreferenceService; five options with most urgent as the default; ordering extends UrgencyCalculator
decisions.why: FR-011 requires the choice be remembered and SC-009 requires it to survive a restart, which rules out mirroring the in-memory BuildingSelectionService; UrgencyCalculator already owns most-urgent-first and is already unit-tested, and every sort key is a value the card already displays so sorting adds no query
decisions.rejected: Mirroring BuildingSelectionService (in-memory, fails SC-009); a per-user database column (puts a display preference in the operational store); a separate sort service (two homes for one ordering rule)

decisions.decision: The Other card gets no Item-selected span: the card is one layout, and the design document full-width Other span is read as a property of the detail-field grid that moves to the request page, where a lone field takes its row full width by field count
decisions.why: FR-006 forbids any layout variant selected by Item, and the checklist already recorded the span as a plan-level layout value rather than a business requirement; deriving it from the declared field count generalises to any odd field count, which the mutable field set requires
decisions.rejected: Special-casing other with RowSpan 2 (a variant selected by Item, and it breaks as soon as other gains a field); width bounds to stretch the lone field (constitution V forbids hardcoded layout boundaries)

decisions.decision: Pictures are keyed by Item under a new request_item scope inheriting a new request_category family scope, reusing config_images_locations and the existing override dialog renamed
decisions.why: FR-009 needs a two-hop Item then Category-family fallback, which is exactly the inheritance shape ImageOverrideDialogViewModel already implements, so storage, read/write services and the batched commit path stay untouched; request_type cannot serve as the Category key because the four Categories are not in RequestTypeInventory
decisions.rejected: Reusing the request_type scope for the Category family (its eight entries are legacy request types, so the key would be a lie); a new Item image table (duplicates ten procedures and the storage root)

decisions.decision: Correct the merged pickup Item rule to require a coil OR flatstock, and drop the dead pickup-flatstock arm
decisions.why: pickup-coil is the CSV merged Pickup row whose source is MMC=>Coil, MMF=>Flatstock and whose visibility requires either, so the current Coil-only rule withholds a supported Item from a flatstock-only job, which SC-004 measures; pickup-flatstock is not one of the 23 pinned Item codes
decisions.rejected: Leaving the rule and seeding no flatstock-only job (SC-004 requires that configuration proven); splitting Pickup back into two Items (the spec pins 23 codes and the merged display name)

plan.summary: Full oversized plan: plan.md with the Constitution Check (six principles, no violations), research.md with 21 Phase 0 decisions, data-model.md reshaping the request and adding the Item configuration entity, and four contract documents covering configuration, picker flow, card, and verification gates.
plan.key_finding: The Category/Item vocabulary is already half-built in code, so this is a re-key onto the store rather than a green field - and the one move that follows from the spec rather than from taste is that the per-Item allotted minutes leave per-Windows-user local settings and become seeded data, because FR-018 must compare the configured value with a history-derived observed average that FR-024 requires to come through a stored procedure.

tasks.summary: 117 tasks across 8 phases (Setup 3, Foundational 29, US1 23, US2 16, US3 11, US4 5, US5 13, Polish 17), laid out as 51 dependency-ordered waves with explicit join points

concerns.note: Seed section 16.4 says the job-independent Item set is six; the spec Edge Case says five after the scrap correction (both Riser Tables, both Hoppers, Other). Resolved in favour of the spec (research D20) - 16.4 is stale, and Scrap is gated on a real scrap decision per FR-031.

Under-specified: Assist has no job-independent Item, so an unfiltered Assist Category on a job with no parts opens an empty Item step, which FR-002 (MUST never be empty) and SC-005 (at least one in every case) forbid. The plan resolves it by filtering the Category list with the same availability pass (research D20). Owner confirmation needed if every Category is instead meant to stay selectable - that would need a job-independent Assist Item, which changes the 23-row catalog the spec pins verbatim.

Seed 16.3 assigns card Line 2 to the code catalog while 16.5 calls it the CSV identifier template, and FR-013s list of what must come from stored configuration excludes the card lines. The plan keeps Line 1 and Line 2 in the code catalog (research D3) and puts only behaviour in the configuration table.

RequestItemPickerRules.RequiredJobPart maps pickup-coil to Coil only, although the CSV row is the merged Pickup item whose source is MMC=>Coil, MMF=>Flatstock and whose visibility requires either - so a flatstock-only job withholds a supported Item (SC-004). The same switch carries a dead pickup-flatstock arm that is not one of the 23 pinned Item codes. Both corrected per research D21.

FR-020 says both configuration screens reuse the role gate that already governs them (singular), but today they are governed by two different gates: CanManageUrgencySettings on the minutes editor and CanManageImageLocationSettings on the picture screen. The plan keeps each screens own gate and collapses neither.
